sources.title: Sources
sources.body:
Nine numerical models come from the Open-Meteo forecast API and one from MET Norway’s Locationforecast, both fetched hourly. The city dashboard places every value on a 6-hour UTC grid (00, 06, 12, 18); the landing overview uses 3-hour slots on the city’s local clock (00, 03, 06…). Temperature, wind and pressure are the values at the step; precipitation is the total of the hours since the previous step.
Regional models return data only inside their domain, so a city outside Europe shows up to eight models. MET Norway publishes hourly values for about the first 60 hours only; later slots use the other models.

median.title: Median and spread
median.body: The median is the middle value of all models that returned data for a step (with an even count, the mean of the two middle values). The dashboard’s bands show the range from the lowest to the highest model and the middle half of the models. Wind direction uses a circular median, so 350° and 10° meet at north. The chance of rain is the share of models forecasting more than {rain} mm in the step.

disagreement.title: Disagreement
disagreement.body: For temperature, wind and pressure the daily disagreement is the average, over the day’s future steps, of the spread between the highest and the lowest model. For precipitation it is the range of the models’ daily totals. Days are in the city’s local time. Thresholds:

limits.title: Limits
limits.body: Model values are grid-point values, not the weather at a street corner. The models are compared with each other, not with what actually happened: measuring which model has been right is a separate feature planned after the MVP. This prototype stores data in local JSON files and caches in memory; the production design uses Postgres, Redis and S3.
